note: P4342 (Pro 29:8-9) — scoffers inflame a city, the wise turn away wrath; arguing with a fool brings no quiet. Two verses.

dims.v: incendiary scorn — scoffers who set a city aflame
the scoffers who set a city aflame — mockery and scorn that inflame a whole community into conflict, the opposite of the wise who turn away wrath
the wise pacifiers they are set against (266927)
set against the wise who turn away wrath

anshe latson (men of scorn / scoffers) — 'SCOFFERS set a city aflame'; scorn is incendiary, inflaming a whole community to strife. Emergent: the scoffer as an arsonist of conflict, against the wise peacemaker (cf 22:10).
peacemaking — the wise who calm the wrath scoffers inflame
the wise who turn away wrath — the peacemaking discernment that calms the anger scoffers inflame, quenching the fire scorn had lit
the scoffers' incendiary scorn it is set against (266924)
set against the scoffers who set a city aflame
chakam (wise) — 'but the WISE turn away wrath'; wisdom is a peacemaker, calming the anger that scorn inflames. Where scoffers kindle, the wise quench (cf 15:1).
unreachable folly — the fool who rages and mocks, giving no quiet
the fool who, when a wise man argues with him, only rages and laughs so that there is no resolution — folly beyond the reach of reasoning, turning debate into noise
welded to the raging and mocking that leaves no quiet

evil (fool) — 'if a wise man has an argument with a FOOL, the fool only rages and laughs'; there is no reasoning with folly — the fool answers argument with rage and mockery, never with quiet. Debating a fool is futile.
turbulence — the fool's raging that admits no resolution
the raging and agitation of the fool in argument — the turbulent anger and mockery that make any quiet resolution impossible, folly's refusal of reasoned peace
the fool whose turbulence it is (266935)
welded to the unreachable folly it expresses
ragaz (rage/be agitated) — 'the fool only RAGES and laughs, and there is no quiet'; the fool meets argument with turbulent rage, so no calm settling is possible. Folly cannot be reasoned to rest.
